newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-GINOLA TO FACE FAMILIAR FRENCH TEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GINOLA TO FACE FAMILIAR FRENCH TEST.

text.p: David Ginola and his Newcastle team-mates will have to overcome French opposition for a second successive round when this season's UEFA Cup reaches the quarter-final stage in March.

After disposing of Metz in the third round, Wednesday's draw pitted the English club against French league leaders Monaco and offered the exiled Ginola another chance to display his attacking skills on French soil.

Newcastle manager Kevin Keegan will be comforted by the statistic that only one English side has been beaten by a French team in European matches, as long ago as 1977 when Bastia beat Newcastle home and away.
But there will be some relief at avoiding Inter Milan, who face Anderlecht, and Monaco technical director Henri Biancheri singled the two sides out as the toughest opponents in the last eight.

"Newcastle was one of the teams we were kind of hoping not to get along with Inter Milan," he said. "But at this level all matches are tough. If we want to go far we have to get through Newcastle, but we have a team that can beat them."
Spanish contenders Tenerife and Valencia have been kept apart, with the former drawn against Danish side Brondby and Valencia tackling Germany's Schalke.

Schalke vice-president Josef Schnusenberg commented: "This is a tough team and perhaps one we might have not wanted to meet. But the players wanted to go to the sun and now they can go and play football."
In the Cup Winners Cup, the big names have also avoided each other, with Fiorentina's clash against Benfica arguably the most attractive tie.
Liverpool and Barcelona have both draw Scandinavian opposition, Norway's Brann Bergen and AIK Stockholm respectively, while Paris St Germain play AEK Athens.
"We know quite a lot about Norwegian football but we don't know this particular club," said Liverpool chief executive Peter Robinson. "We do have a Norwegian, Stig Bjornebye, and he'll be our scout."
